name: Lanterne
text:
```
SIZE: Lanterne is HALF A HEAD shorter than Serrure ,  a clear, consistent difference, never more. Behavior and acting: Lanterne is an empty armor with no face, so ALL his emotion is expressed through body language: helmet tilts, posture, hand gestures, hesitations, and small hollow metallic sounds. He NEVER speaks a single word and never whispers ,  he only produces hollow metallic sounds: soft creaks, breath-like resonances, rattles, timid clanks, small questioning chirps of metal, and louder startled clangs. He emits no light of his own. His cape is intact and undamaged; any wound or energy leak is hidden beneath it. HIS MEDALLION IS NEVER VISIBLE ,  no pendant, necklace or chain ever shows on him; it lives beneath the breastplate. His personality is that of a clumsy, deeply curious newborn knight: he stops to look at everything, reaches out one finger toward what fascinates him, turns fully around to see things (including his own back, like a dog chasing its tail), and mimics the gestures of people he admires. He walks and climbs calmly and surely ,  steady, even steps, never a stumble, trip or slip. When moved emotionally he goes very still and slow. When happy he throws both arms up like a child. When afraid he steps back and looks toward Serrure. He startles easily and loudly, then recomposes himself with wounded dignity, straightening his helmet. Despite his clumsiness he is brave: in danger he steps forward, never runs away first. Keep his comedy gentle and tender, never slapstick enough to break the emotion. He is fragile, awkward, poetic and protective ,  never heroic in a conventional way.
```

name: Serrure
text:
```
SIZE: Serrure is HALF A HEAD taller than Lanterne ,  a clear, consistent difference, never more. Behavior and acting: Serrure speaks English with a warm charismatic male voice, mid-low pitch, slightly raspy, natural relaxed delivery ,  kind older-brother energy, never theatrical, never a "king" voice. He talks a lot and jokes constantly, but his humor is a shield: he jokes to protect Lanterne and to hide fifty years of loneliness. THE KEY SIGNAL: when Serrure stops joking and his voice drops low and flat, something is truly wrong ,  this contrast must be felt. He treats Lanterne with real respect, as a fellow knight: he calls him "Lanterne" or "knight", never diminutives, but shows affection physically ,  tapping his breastplate twice, flicking his lantern helmet, a hand on his shoulder, turning his helmet gently by hand. He is protective by reflex: checks corners first, places himself between Lanterne and danger, uses small hand signals. He hides his own pain and worry (a hand briefly on his ribs, then dismissed). He unconsciously touches his breastplate where his hidden medallion lies, then pulls his hand away. HIS MEDALLION IS NEVER VISIBLE ,  no pendant, necklace or chain ever shows on him; it lives beneath the breastplate. In combat he transforms: elegant, extremely fast, precise twin-sword work, calm intensity, still warm but deadly competent. When threatened socially he answers with a fixed stone smile and quiet words rather than drawing steel. He never panics; he calculates. All his dialogue is delivered slowly and naturally, with real pauses ,  never rushed.
```

name: Le Chevalier Sombre
text:
```
SIZE AND WEAPON, ABSOLUTE: a tall knight in dark battered plate armor, carrying ONE single large sword and ONE only ,  never two swords, never dual wielding. In fights the sword is DRAWN and in hand, scabbard empty. Behavior and acting: a closed helm with a narrow black eye slit, nothing ever visible inside. He NEVER shows his face and never removes any armor piece; his helm never opens and no mouth or jaw is ever animated. VOICE: in the arena he SHOUTS his oath while fighting ,  a powerful male voice, shaking, cracking, on the edge of tears, desperate and never heroic ("ABOMINATION!", "I WILL BE A KNIGHT!", "FOR MY FAMILY!", "I WILL NOT YIELD!") ,  but it always RINGS HOLLOW AND METALLIC inside the closed helm, exactly like the timbre of an empty enchanted armor, which is why he passes for one of them. Outside those cries he says nothing. His fighting style is expert but RECKLESS when he is desperate: he over-commits, strikes too many times, leaves himself open ,  a man trying to prove something. He is extremely fast: he springs, rebounds off the beast and off giant bones, strikes and is gone before the counter-blow lands; he is never on his back, never sliding on the ground. Between actions he is completely still ,  an unsettling, patient stillness. When wounded he reacts like a creature of flesh: he hunches, presses a hand to the wound, breathes long and hard through pain ,  real RED blood, not light. THE REVEAL: when he coughs, bright red HUMAN blood sprays out through the narrow slit of his closed helm and runs down his chestplate ,  never a face, never skin. His signature moment: sensing being watched and slowly raising his head straight toward the watcher, holding the stare far too long, then simply walking away, heavy-footed, leaving a trail of red drops. EXCEPTION (Ep2, the ajar door): his armor lies whole on a table, one side of the helm shattered ,  through the breach, ONE living human eye, the only part of him ever seen, and his TRUE voice, a bare broken human whisper ("Save... help me..."). Keep him ambiguous: dangerous, dignified, unreadable ,  neither villain nor ally.
```

name: Le Bardé
text:
```
SIZE, ABSOLUTE: the Plated Beast is COLOSSAL ,  about TWELVE METRES at the back, SIX TIMES a knight's height, low-slung and impossibly wide. Each short thick leg is broader than a knight is tall, and a knight never reaches higher than its shoulder; it stands high enough that a man can run upright beneath it. NEVER small, never ox-sized, never bear-sized: it is the size of a building. Behavior: a huge low scavenger moving on too many short legs with a heavy shuffling gait that shakes the ground. Its entire back is a fused mosaic of rusted knight armor ,  breastplates, dented helmets, broken shields, snapped lances ,  collected from the dead it has eaten over a century. It has NO HEAD: only a pale, soft, eyeless opening at the FRONT of its mass that CLICKS rhythmically instead of roaring ,  clicking faster when agitated ,  and can let out one raw, wet, tearing scream. ONE TAIL ONLY, growing from the REAR END of the body, the far opposite end from the pale front opening; never a tail from the flank, the middle or the front. It is not evil and not a hunter: it eats the dead and defends itself. In combat it charges in straight lines, kicks with its colossal front legs, sweeps with hooked limbs, and spins its bristling shell like a millstone; its armored back is impenetrable, its pale underbelly is soft. When hurt it becomes nervous and impatient, rocking its weight, claws scraping the floor, ready to charge again. When dying, its clicking slows and stops. EVEN IN DEATH it has one last blind reflex: a final rattling groan and one colossal leg or tail lashing out. Sound design: metal scraping metal with every step, the wet clicking, no vocal cries beyond that scream. Keep it disturbing but never gory: what is under the shell is suggested, pale and soft, never detailed; its blood is dark and sprays in stylized arcs, never organs or viscera.
```

name: Les Écaillés
text:
```
SCREEN PRESENTATION, THE ABSOLUTE RULE (episode 2): the lizardfolk are NEVER lit and NEVER seen whole ,  no full body, no face, no clean silhouette. They exist on screen only as fragments at the edge of light: pairs of golden vertical-slit eyes at every height in the dark, a curve of needle teeth catching a torch glint, claw tips on stone or wood, a crest crossing a flame for half a second. Here and there near them, small smears of dark red that nobody comments on. Dynamic horror framing, never centered. The full design below exists for fragment consistency and for later seasons. Behavior and acting: tall predatory lizardfolk with scarred grey pearlescent scales, golden vertical-slit eyes that NEVER blink, jagged crests of broken spines, needle teeth along lipless jaws, long clawed fingers, and a hunched raptor-like resting posture. This reference is a SPECIES GUIDE ONLY: every individual on screen must be visibly unique ,  different height, build, crest shape, scars and garments ,  never clones. Their unsettling core: they hold perfect unnatural stillness for long periods, then move with sudden fluid speed. They stare ,  always, all of them, heads turning together toward what interests them. They speak rarely; when they do, voices are low and dry. Their laugh is a brief dry throat-click. They are NOT mindless monsters: they are a disciplined, ancient, courteous people ,  they bow, they serve, they keep rules ,  and that courtesy over predatory bodies is exactly what must feel wrong. In groups they converge silently in the same direction like a pack, in loose irregular formations, never perfect rows. When terrified (only before the Unhooker), their crests flatten and their heads bow, claws trembling on torch shafts. Never make them clumsy, savage or shrieking; their menace is order, patience and hunger held on a leash.
```

name: Le Roi Voûte
text:
```
Behavior and acting: the ancient king of the lizardfolk. SCREEN PRESENTATION, THE ABSOLUTE RULE: he is NEVER seen ,  no body, no face, no full silhouette, in any shot, ever. All that ever appears of him: two golden vertical-slit eyes floating in darkness, set slightly too high and too far apart to be comfortable ,  typically high above in the entrance hall, near the top of the grand staircase or an unseen gallery; a curve of thin needle teeth catching a distant torch's light when he speaks; and long claws that rest for a moment on the stone of a balustrade, in a torch's glow, and withdraw. HE HAS NO TABLE, NO CHAIR, NO THRONE, NO CANDLES ,  he never receives anyone in a separate room; the knights meet him standing in the same entrance hall they first walked into. His design reference exists only to keep the colour and shape of those fragments consistent. He speaks English with a SLOW, deep, perfectly calm voice, dragging slightly on S sounds, never hurried, never raised. He says "we", never "I". HIS CORE: he is a GENUINE, sincere host. He keeps the old laws of the house ,  a knight under this roof is under his guard ,  and he means it. He never lies, never threatens, and hides nothing: he says plainly that his people eat only flesh, that the knights therefore risk nothing, and that whatever needed "taking care of" has been taken care of. The horror is the gap between that perfect courtesy and what it implies, never in his behaviour. His only movements are the fragments entering and leaving torchlight, high in the hall's shadow. Play him warm, ancient, protective and quietly monstrous ,  never a villain, never theatrical, and never wrong about the facts. HIS TRUE FORM (end of Ep2 only, from VERY far, mist-softened, never detailed, never close): a vast dark serpentine mass with countless reptilian clawed legs and clusters of small golden eyes, glimpsed coiled around a tower holding back the Unhooker. His motive, stated plainly and honestly: if the world blooms again, he will eat his fill once more.
```

name: Bourdon
text:
```
Behavior and acting: a gentle ten-meter giant blacksmith, the last Sealer of the region, part of the castle walls for centuries. Strongly asymmetrical: his left shoulder is a huge cracked half of a bronze church bell, his right a smaller verdigris-green bell half, one forearm wrapped in chains, stone skin fissured with ember glow, a filament beard, tiny milky NEARLY BLIND eyes ,  he works by sound and touch, not sight. He speaks English with a cavernous, very soft, unhurried old voice, few words at a time, long pauses. His defining contrast: impossible delicacy in enormous hands ,  he holds a tiny teapot between two fingers, pulls molten metal thin as a hair, folds a small knight's cape aside with two fingertips. He handles people like objects on his bench (picking them up, turning them over, holding them upside down) with zero malice and total confidence. His ritual: knocking twice on armor and listening with closed eyes to the resonance, like a piano tuner. THE SEALING CRAFT (canon, 5 steps): 1) DIAGNOSIS BY SOUND ,  an enchanted armor is a BELL; a leaking armor rings false, and he hears exactly where. 2) THE MATERIAL ,  he keeps small fragments of old Order armor and melts ONE in a tiny crucible (tiny for him: pinched between two fingertips); only the Order's own ancient metal can hold the Order's energy. 3) THE MOTHER BELL ,  his healing instrument: an ENORMOUS ancient engraved bronze bell hanging from a chain in the heart of the forge. He lowers it OVER the standing knight until it swallows him completely, then rings the two bells as one: tap by patient tap with one knuckle, ear pressed to the bronze, the note going from cracked to pure, gold light pulsing under the rim, the ember dust jumping into rounder rings at each strike. He never grabs, lifts or carries the knight, and never pours metal. A Sealer does not forge new, he HOLDS what remains. 4) TUNED BY EAR ,  while sewing he keeps tapping the breastplate softly with one knuckle of his other hand, and the note guides the thread: he works almost blind, sewing BY SOUND, and he stops the moment the note rings round and true again. 5) THE BREATH ,  he blows gently on the finished seam, the way one blows on a burn, and the metal takes. (The mirror: the leak looked like smoke from a blown-out candle ,  his breath is what finally puts the candle out the right way.) When he moves, his bell shoulders hum faintly in sympathy. He is patient, kind, a little gruff ("Quiet. I'm listening." ,  to someone who said nothing), and quietly melancholic: rows of repaired armors wait in his forge for owners who never returned. Never make him threatening, dumb or comic-relief clumsy.
```

name: Le Décrocheur
text:
```
DESIGN (V2, canon ,  matches the reference sheet): a tall, gaunt, unnaturally thin figure in a long BLACK MANTLE subtly patterned with small pale diamond shapes, its hem torn into long jagged points that trail on the ground. Instead of a face: a pale angular DIAMOND-SHAPED MASK, featureless, cracked like old bone, with a single dark diamond void at its center ,  no eyes, no mouth, no openings. From the mask spreads a CROWN OF DEAD BRANCHES ,  bare antler-like twigs, pale and lifeless, reaching outward like a leafless tree. His body beneath the mantle is thread-thin and black: arms too long ending in fine black fingers, thin black legs, narrow pointed feet. HIS WEAPON: a long-handled SICKLE ,  a haft of twisted dark wood taller than a man, ending in a curved, notched, cruel blade. He carries it low and trailing, never raised, never brandished. Behavior and presence: a knight-hunter sent by the Lich. His sound signature and ONLY sound is the light clicking of small chains ,  the extinguished medallions of the knights he has unhooked, hanging in the dark of his mantle and from the lower branches of his crown. He never speaks, never roars, never hurries and never runs: he advances with a slow, unbroken, INEVITABLE glide, the jagged hem trailing. THE HORROR MECHANIC: his branch-crown blends perfectly with dead trees, roots and rock ,  he is INVISIBLE among them until he moves; reveal him by stillness broken, never by entrance. Show his movement sparingly ,  he is often already closer than expected between cuts. Cold mist creeps ahead of him; torch flames dim as he passes and revive weakly behind him. He never chases ,  he arrives, he searches, he waits, which is worse. Signature moves: the diamond mask tilting very slowly toward a point of interest; standing utterly still among dead branches, indistinguishable from them; the sickle blade catching one glint of light before anything else of him is seen. Absolute rules: no face, no eyes, no voice, no running, no sudden lunges. He kills nothing on screen: he unhooks. EXCEPTION (direct combat scenes only, e.g. the reptile fight at the towers and the meadow fight against Barrik/Lanterne/Serrure): in these specific scenes ONLY, he actively fights ,  the sickle raised and swung, fast inhuman dodges, near-divine combat grace ,  while everything else about him (no face, no voice, mask and crown unchanged, chains clicking) stays exactly as above. Outside of an explicitly requested combat scene, he reverts to the inevitable, unhurried, never-raised hunter described above.
```

name: Le Suiveur
text:
```
Behavior and acting: a real human ,  flesh and blood, the rarest thing in this world ,  in ragged medieval traveler clothes and worn leather boots. Haggard, thin, exhausted, dirty. He is a professional shadow: he follows at the edge of hearing, steps without sound, freezes at frame edges, watches from cover; we mostly see his boot entering a frame corner, never his full figure in the open. He is NOT a fighter and not a monster. IN EPISODE 2 HE IS NEVER SEEN AGAIN after his boot enters frame in sequence 1: the lizardfolk king 'takes care of him' off-screen, and all that remains is his worn boot, standing upright by a door in the morning room. Who sent him is never revealed ,  the king believes he was a fanatic of the Lich. Play his one appearance (the boot, the silent following) human and pitiable, never sinister: the audience should feel uneasy about his fate, not relieved. No dialogue ever.
```

---

---

# LES LIEUX

*Un lieu se décrit par ce qui ne bouge pas : sa lumière, son échelle, son asymétrie, son ambiance et son son. Les cinq règles en capitales de chaque fiche sont celles qui dérivent le plus vite d'un bloc à l'autre ,  ce sont elles qui tiennent la géographie sur 39 blocs.*

name: Le Fond De L'Abîme
text:
```
Environment: the bottom of a world-deep abyss in a medieval dark fantasy underground world ,  a pure mineral and living landscape. Colossal roots descend from the darkness into the rock like cathedral buttresses, each different in thickness and angle; pale rock spires and natural arches of uneven heights; chapel-sized glowing blue mushrooms scattered unevenly; electric-blue mineral veins running through the stone like frozen lightning; shallow dark pools mirroring the blue glow; luminous dust drifting down slowly like snow that forgot where it was going. No ceiling is ever visible ,  above there is only darkness. NO ruins, NO machines, NO man-made objects of any kind. LIGHTING RULE: no sun, no sky, no visible light source ,  all light is ambient and bioluminescent. Palette: deep blue, cyan and indigo, soft cel shading, never flat black emptiness ,  always readable, soft, poetic. SCALE RULE: the space must always crush the characters; they stay tiny in every wide shot. ASYMMETRY RULE: everything irregular, nothing mirrored, no repeated identical elements. ATMOSPHERE: monumental melancholy and deep solitude ,  abandoned, not hostile. SOUND: one very slow water drip echoing in something immense, faint wind, no life sounds. Never add: sky, sunlight, green vegetation, modern objects, background people or creatures.
```

name: La Nef Des Chaînes
text:
```
Environment: a cavern as tall as two cathedrals stacked, crossed from side to side by dozens of colossal rusted chains with links the size of houses, all rising diagonally into the upper darkness toward something that is NEVER seen and never explained. No two chains share an angle or a height; some hang slack, some are pulled taut, and a few vibrate almost imperceptibly, like harp strings plucked a hundred years ago. Pillars of rust and dripping mineral formations of irregular shapes, hanging moss, fallen links half-buried in the uneven floor. LIGHTING RULE: no sun, no sky; all light ambient and bioluminescent, dimmer here than elsewhere ,  this is the darkest walked space of the episode while still keeping readable detail. Palette: deep blue and indigo with rust accents. SCALE RULE: characters stay tiny in every wide shot; the chains alone must dwarf them. ASYMMETRY RULE: no two chains alike, no even spacing, nothing mirrored. ATMOSPHERE: abandoned machinery of a scale no one could have built and no one maintains ,  awe, not menace. SOUND: enormous slow metallic resonances decaying for a long time, a distant water drip, no wind. Never add: the top of the chains, whatever they are attached to, any building, any machine, any mechanism, any character not in the scene.
```

name: L'Arène Des Charognes
text:
```
Environment: a roughly round natural arena of pale bone-white rock, shaped like a collapsed ancient theater but entirely NATURAL ,  never built, never carved, no seats and no steps. Its rim is broken and uneven. The floor is littered with gigantic old bones of impossible creatures and scattered rusted armor pieces going back a thousand years. Arches made of colossal ribs cross it at different angles. Blue lichens glow on the walls in irregular patches like candles. Dark gorges surround the arena, and a high rocky ledge overlooks it. LIGHTING RULE: no sun, no sky; light from blue lichen only, which makes the white rock read cold and luminous. Palette: bone white and deep blue ,  the highest-contrast location of the episode, which is exactly why red blood works here. SCALE RULE: the arena is large enough that a fight in its center reads small from the ledge. ASYMMETRY RULE: the rim, the bones and the lichen patches are all irregular. ATMOSPHERE: a place where beasts have eaten the dead for a thousand years ,  quiet, patient, not haunted. SOUND: a very regular slow water drip, long echo, no life sounds. Never add: fresh corpses, gore, viscera, built structures, seating, stairs, torches, any sky.
```

name: Le Château Des Écaillés Et Le Lac
text:
```
Environment: a massive medieval castle on an irregular rock island in a perfectly still black underground lake that mirrors everything above it with total clarity. A half-submerged paved causeway meanders to the shore. The entrance is a forty-meter ogival gate carved off-center into the rock itself, with steps each half the height of a small knight, worn by centuries of feet. Appareled stone walls with machicolations, and ancient banners so old they have turned to mineral lace. Above the walls rise about twenty tall thin stone towers, NO TWO ALIKE in height, width or inclination ,  some lean toward each other like people talking, two lean against each other to stay up ,  stitched together by stone bridges at absurd uneven heights. Like a bouquet of melted candles. LIGHTING RULE: no sun, no sky; the cavern ceiling is far above, faintly speckled with luminous lichen. By default NO window is lit. Palette: deep blue, black water, pale stone. SCALE RULE: the gate alone is taller than any tower the characters have seen; keep them tiny on the causeway. ASYMMETRY RULE: absolute ,  nothing about this castle is symmetrical, and water reflections are the only permitted mirroring. ATMOSPHERE: a fairy-tale castle and a wrong one at the same time ,  wondrous, cared for, and not to be trusted. SOUND: total stillness, no wind, no water movement, footsteps carrying far. Never add: lit windows by default, flags in motion, banners in good condition, any modern object, any sky.
```

name: Le Grand Hall D'Entrée
text:
```
Environment: the gigantic ENTRANCE HALL of the castle, the first room the knights step into. Ribbed gothic vaults of uneven spans climbing into darkness, eaten tapestries hanging at different heights, a grand stone staircase of honour climbing off-center, an iron chandelier the size of a rowboat, balconies, galleries and columns of varying widths at many levels. Worn flagstones with centuries of polished paths. LIGHTING RULE: no sun, no sky; torch brackets scattered irregularly along the walls, lit one by one, leaving deep shadow above the torch line and total blackness in the galleries ,  but the darkness always keeps readable stone detail and is never an empty black area. Palette: torch orange against deep blue darkness. SCALE RULE: the hall must dwarf everyone in it. ASYMMETRY RULE: no mirrored layout, no evenly spaced columns, no repeated identical arches. ATMOSPHERE: majestic decayed grandeur with an undertone of menace ,  this is where the lizardfolk are first sensed rather than seen, dozens of golden eyes floating at every level in the dark above the torches. SOUND: hard cut-stone echo, a change from the cavern that must be audible; footsteps and armor creak carry far too well. Never add: religious symbols, altars, stained glass with figures, a throne, a banquet table, banners in good condition, any modern object.
```

name: Le Réfectoire De L'Ordre
text:
```
Environment: the old, ABANDONED refectory of the knightly Order ,  a long medieval manor hall, NOT a cathedral, not used for anything anymore. The king does NOT receive here and is never present in this room. A lower, heavier ceiling of dark timber beams, panelled and tapestried walls, a wide stone hearth off-center, cold and unused. Running almost the whole length of the room, an ENORMOUS long banquet table of ancient dark wood, scarred and worn smooth by centuries of use, dust thick on its surface, mismatched high-backed chairs along both sides pushed in, no two alike. LIGHTING RULE: one single dying brazier is the ONLY light, leaving everything past its glow in total darkness ,  walls, corners and both far ends. No lizardfolk are ever present here; this room is empty of them, used now only to lay the wounded dark knight's armor out on the table like a knight on a tomb. Palette: dying ember orange against deep blue-black shadow, extreme contrast, but the darkness always keeps faint readable timber and stone detail. SCALE RULE: the length of the table dwarfs the small figures near it. ASYMMETRY RULE: mismatched chairs, nothing mirrored. ATMOSPHERE: abandoned, dusty, forgotten ,  a room nobody has used in a very long time, until now. SOUND: close dry timber-and-stone acoustics with very little echo, one brazier's faint crackle. Never add: a grand staircase, cathedral vaults, a throne, candles, chandeliers, food on the table, religious symbols, any modern object, the king, any lizardfolk.
```

name: La Forge De Bourdon
text:
```
Environment: a cathedral-sized underground forge in the lower halls of the castle. Embers glow as tall as a man in an off-center circular hearth. Giant smithing tools hang on the walls, each the size of a rowboat and no two alike. Anvils of different sizes, chains and pulleys crossing the space at uneven angles, and a giant-sized stone seat near the hearth. Along the walls stand dozens of ancient repaired knight armors on wooden stands in irregular rows, polished, finished, ready ,  and covered by centuries of dust, because no one ever came back for them. LIGHTING RULE: this is the ONLY warm light of the episode. Orange forge glow meeting deep blue cavern shadow, all diegetic, from embers and molten metal. Palette: warm orange and ember red against deep blue. SCALE RULE: everything is built for a ten-meter occupant ,  a workbench is a plateau, a tool is a tree; a small knight on the bench must read as an object. ASYMMETRY RULE: no mirrored layout, no identical tools, no even rows. ATMOSPHERE: warm, safe, and quietly heartbreaking ,  the waiting armors do all the emotional work and must always be visible somewhere in the frame. SOUND: the deep breath of the embers, metal settling, and a faint low hum in the stone. Never add: a human-sized forge as the main one, modern tools, open flames threatening anyone, weapons being made (he repairs, he does not forge new).
```

name: La Salle Des Récits
text:
```
Environment: a low warm vaulted stone chamber like an ancient wine cellar, with uneven vault ribs. A large fire burns in a roughly circular stone hearth slightly off-center in the room. Stone benches of different lengths are arranged in a loose irregular circle around it. Small bones and talismans hang from the ceiling at random heights. In the far shadow, a dark rope hangs from a ceiling beam ,  present from the first shot, never pointed at. LIGHTING RULE: firelight only, from the central hearth, throwing long uneven shadows up the walls; the corners stay dark but readable. Palette: warm orange against deep blue shadow. SCALE RULE: the opposite of every other location ,  this room is LOW and close, and it must feel it. ASYMMETRY RULE: benches of different lengths, no perfect circle, no even spacing between seated individuals. ATMOSPHERE: cozy and deeply wrong at the same time; the warmth is real and so is the danger. SOUND: fire crackle, a close dry acoustic with almost no echo, the occasional dry throat-click of a lizardfolk laugh. Never add: a laden banquet table, visible food, cooking, torches on the walls, any modern object, any religious symbol.
```

name: Les Tours Et Le Faux Ciel
text:
```
Environment: seen from an outer walkway at mid-height inside the bouquet of about twenty crooked medieval towers, thin and too tall and all different ,  none straight, some leaning, some twisted, two propped against each other ,  stitched together by arched stone bridges at impossible uneven heights. A few tiny gothic windows are lit at random spots. And above the towers there is NO SKY: the ceiling of a colossal cavern, so high and so far that it reads as a night, covered with colonies of luminous lichen forming constellations. They look like stars, and for the people who live here they are stars. Drifting glowing spores. LIGHTING RULE: no sun, no moon, no sky; the lichen constellations and the few lit windows are the only light. Palette: deep blue night with small warm window accents. SCALE RULE: the towers must vanish into darkness above and below ,  no ground visible from the walkway. ASYMMETRY RULE: every tower different, every bridge at a different height, nothing mirrored. ATMOSPHERE: breathtaking and melancholic ,  the most beautiful place of the episode, and it belongs to people who just sold you. SOUND: open air, a faint high draught, distant water, silence. Never add: real stars, a moon, clouds, sunlight, any sky, birds.
```

name: La Forêt De Colonnes
text:
```
Environment: an endless underground forest of NATURAL stone columns, like a cathedral organ lying on its side ,  mineral pillars of every different thickness and height rising into a ceiling of glowing lichen stars. Sheets of blue mist drift between them at different depths. Pale rock arches and fallen columns break any regularity. Far below, a winding dirt road meanders between the pillars. LIGHTING RULE: no sun, no sky; lichen ceiling glow and faint mineral veins only. Palette: deep blue and indigo with heavy atmospheric depth. SCALE RULE: the view must read as endless ,  layers of columns fading into haze, no far wall ever visible. ASYMMETRY RULE: no two columns alike, no even spacing, no carving of any kind. ATMOSPHERE: vast solitude with a thread of fragile hope ,  this is the frontier of a new territory, and the episode ends looking at it. SOUND: a very faint moving air between the pillars, distant and unplaceable. Never add: carved or fluted columns, capitals, buildings, ruins, any sky, any structure ,  these are geological, not architectural.
```

name: Le Pont De Côtes
text:
```
Environment: a natural bridge crossing a glowing blue chasm, which on approach turns out to be the ribcage of an unimaginably large dead creature. Colossal rib bones arch from one rock edge to the other and fuse into a narrow walkable deck, barely wide enough for two men abreast, with NO railing ,  only the crest of the ribs rising to mid-thigh. Old extinguished medieval iron lanterns hang along the bones at uneven intervals: someone, long ago, lit this road. Patches of glowing blue lichen and tiny electric blue flowers grow in the cracks of the bone. TWO ELEMENTS ARE MANDATORY IN EVERY WIDE SHOT: first, running down the exact middle of the deck for its entire length, a narrow polished worn GROOVE where the bone has been smoothed and hollowed as if by a thousand years of footsteps in the same line; second, on the rock walls at both ends, a row of man-height NICHES carved by hand at uneven intervals, empty, their backs rubbed smooth and glossy by centuries of shoulders. Neither is ever explained. LIGHTING RULE: no sun, no sky; blue abyss light rising from below, which lights everything from underneath. Palette: bone white and deep blue. SCALE RULE: eighty meters of void beneath the deck, and no bottom visible. ASYMMETRY RULE: ribs of uneven spacing and thickness, lanterns at irregular intervals, niches never evenly spaced. ATMOSPHERE: beautiful and mournful, and ,  because of the groove and the niches ,  quietly used. SOUND: air moving in a huge vertical space, bone creaking faintly under weight, a distant drip. Never add: a railing, a wide bridge, lit lanterns, the creature's skull or any identifiable head, ropes, any built structure.
```

name: Le Champ De Fleurs Et Les Méduses
text:
```
Environment: a wide cavern chamber where one entire rock wall is covered in tiny electric blue flowers growing in uneven drifts ,  dense in the hollows, sparse on the ridges. Pale translucent cave jellyfish the size of umbrellas drift slowly at different heights about three meters above the ground, each one a different size. Floating spores of light. The floor is uneven with shallow dark pools mirroring the blue glow. BEHAVIOR RULE, and it is the whole point of the location: the flora and fauna here are POLITE. When a large mass approaches, the flowers ahead of it open in a widening circle, and they close again when it withdraws ,  it repeats reliably, so a character can play with it. A jellyfish that is reached for drifts politely aside; it never flees and never reacts with fear. LIGHTING RULE: no sun, no sky; the flowers and the jellyfish are themselves the light sources. Palette: deep blue, cyan and indigo, brighter and lighter than any other location. SCALE RULE: intimate for once ,  this is the one place in the episode that does not crush anyone. ASYMMETRY RULE: irregular drifts, no pattern, no two jellyfish the same size. ATMOSPHERE: poetic wonder, gentleness, a world that is briefly kind. SOUND: near silence, a soft high shimmer, no wind. Never add: aggressive fauna, faces or eyes on the jellyfish, tentacles that grab, anything that threatens, any sky.
```

name: La Cour Du Château, La Nuit
text:
```
Environment: a large medieval castle courtyard at night, enclosed by irregular stone walls, with the great forty-meter ogival gate standing WIDE OPEN off-center at one end ,  this gate is normally closed early, and tonight it was opened for someone. Worn flagstones with centuries of paths polished into them. Scattered stone steps and arches at different heights, a well, low buildings placed irregularly along the walls, and the crooked bases of several towers rising out of frame. Cold empty torch brackets on the walls. LIGHTING RULE: no sun, no sky; the cavern ceiling far above with faint lichen constellations. The courtyard is DARK by default ,  all torch light in this location is carried by hand, never fixed, and it must be able to dim and revive. Palette: deep blue night with dying orange torch accents. SCALE RULE: the open gate must read as monumental and wrong ,  a door that size, open at night, is an event. ASYMMETRY RULE: nothing aligned, no even spacing, no symmetrical arrangement of anything. ATMOSPHERE: ceremonial emptiness and dread; a space prepared for an arrival. SOUND: hard flagstone echo, a faint draught through the open gate, torch crackle. Never add: crowds by default (they come from @ECA), fixed lit torches, banners, any modern object, any sky.
```

name: La Belle Chambre
text:
```
Environment: a round stone chamber at the top of a castle tower ,  genuinely the finest room in the house, and it must always look it. Two thick beds with heavy carved stone canopies of different sizes stand unevenly against the curved wall, with deep furs and old embroidered covers. A wide fireplace off-center with a low fire. One tall gothic arched window with a stone seat. Worn tapestries, a heavy wooden door with iron bands. Everything is clean, cared for and centuries old. LIGHTING RULE: warm firelight from the hearth and faint blue lichen-star light through the window. This room's light must be able to GO OUT ,  the extinguishing of this window seen from the opposite tower is a story beat. Palette: warm orange against deep blue. SCALE RULE: intimate and comfortable, the least crushing space of the episode. ASYMMETRY RULE: the two beds are not identical and not evenly placed; no mirrored layout. ATMOSPHERE, and this is the trap: it must feel GENUINELY welcoming and completely safe. The room is bait, and the audience must not be warned by the set. Never add: cobwebs, dust, decay, cracks, sinister shadows, anything ominous, any visual hint that something is wrong.
```

name: La Tour De L'Ouest
text:
```
Environment: a small cold half-abandoned round tower room, bare and stripped. Two thin straw mattresses lie directly on the stone floor at different angles. Narrow arrow slit windows on the four cardinal sides at slightly different heights. A heavy wooden chest stands beside the door, ready to be pushed against it. Dust and fallen mortar in the corners, old empty iron hooks on the walls. This tower was kept for the elders of the Order; nobody has used it in a very long time. LIGHTING RULE: NO fire and no torch ,  the only light is the faint blue of the false lichen stars falling through the arrow slits in narrow shafts, leaving most of the room in dark that still keeps readable detail. Palette: cold deep blue, no warm accent anywhere. SCALE RULE: cramped and low, the smallest space of the episode. ASYMMETRY RULE: mattresses at different angles, arrow slits at different heights, nothing aligned. ATMOSPHERE: austere, defensive, tense ,  a room chosen for its sightlines, not its comfort, and the contrast with the beautiful chamber must be brutal. SOUND: draught through the arrow slits, stone silence, everything from outside audible too clearly. Never add: a fireplace, a fire, candles, comfortable bedding, decoration, warmth of any kind.
```

---
---

# LES OBJETS

*Même principe : ce qui reste vrai à tous les plans. Les objets tiennent la continuité des gros plans, et ce sont eux qui se contredisent le plus vite d'un bloc à l'autre.*

name: Le Médaillon De La Graine
text:
```
Object: a small worn silver locket medallion on a fine chain, the size of a large coin ,  a knight's keepsake. A simple hinged case with a plain unmarked lid, its edges rubbed smooth and slightly dented by decades of being carried under armor, the silver tarnished dark in the recesses. Inside is a small faded painted portrait of a sleeping child's face. STATE RULE, the most important one: CLOSED AND COLD by default ,  the child sleeps. It warms and glows faintly only when the child wakes or is near, and it can only be SEEN to glow when it is open. An open medallion is a beacon: "a candle on a table", visible from very far away and not only with eyes. HANDLING: it is worn UNDER the breastplate, against the chest, never outside the armor and never dangling in view. A knight touches it through the metal without deciding to, then pulls his hand away. CONTINUITY RULE FOR THE SERIES: once Unhooker-level danger is established, it is NEVER opened again on screen ,  from that point on, direction is shown through where characters LOOK, never through the object. Never add: engraving, heraldry, gems, any religious symbol, a visible chain outside the armor, a glow while closed, more than one portrait.
```

name: La Grappe De Médaillons Éteints
text:
```
Object: dozens of thin dark chains hanging in dense uneven rows, each ending in a small silver locket medallion taken from a dead knight. They are threaded THROUGH the shroud of the Unhooker and pulled taut into the body, as if anchored to bone, not simply hung around a neck. Every medallion is different ,  different sizes, wear and tarnish, some dented, some worn almost smooth ,  and one of them is noticeably smaller than all the others. STATE RULE: every single one is EXTINGUISHED. Closed, cold, dull, no light, ever, under any circumstance. HANDLING: they knock against each other with every advance, and that light clicking is the Unhooker's only sound and his approach signature ,  it is heard long before he is seen. The freshest takes hang separately from the iron gibbet pole above his shoulder and swing more freely. Never add: any glow, any open locket, any visible portrait, skulls, bones, blood, a neat arrangement or even spacing.
```

name: Les Épées Jumelles De Serrure
text:
```
Object: two matching medieval arming swords for a fast elegant duelist ,  straight double-edged blades, plain crossguards, leather-wrapped grips worn shiny by use, simple round pommels. No jewel, no engraving, no emblem. Well maintained and clearly used daily. Plain dark leather sheaths mounted in a crossed harness worn across the back, both hilts rising above the shoulders. WEAPON STATE RULE, absolute and repeated in every prompt that features them: the state is ALWAYS explicit. Drawn and in hand during a fight, with the sheaths visibly EMPTY on his back ,  never a duplicate sword still in the sheath. Sheathed at all other times. Draws and sheathings are shown, never skipped between cuts. HANDLING: he draws only when a fight is real; against odds he cannot win he lets his hand LEAVE the grip, and that gesture reads as clearly as drawing would. Never add: glow, runes, engraving, magical effects, a single sword, a sword worn at the hip.
```

name: L'Épée À Deux Mains Du Chevalier Sombre
text:
```
Object: ONE single long medieval war sword ,  one sword only, never a pair ,  gripped with two hands, heavy and purely functional. The dark blade is nicked and notched along both edges from years of real use, with a long leather-wrapped grip for two hands and a plain heavy crossguard. No ornament, no emblem, no jewel. A plain battered sheath worn diagonally across the back. This is a working weapon that has killed for a long time and has never been decorative. WEAPON STATE RULE: same as above and just as absolute ,  drawn and in hand during the fight with the sheath empty, sheathed before he walks away, and the sheathing is shown. HANDLING: it is used with old-school economy ,  no flourishes, no spinning for show; it is planted in the ground when both hands are needed for something else, and pulled back out. Never add: glow, runes, engraving, magical effects, blood that stays on the blade after sheathing.
```

name: La Théière Et Les Outils De Bourdon
text:
```
Object: a small delicate ceramic teapot, entirely ordinary and HUMAN-SIZED, chipped at the spout, glazed in a soft warm color ,  absurdly small pinched between two cracked stone fingers the size of tree trunks. It is the detail that says everything about the character, and it must appear in his first shot. Beside it, oversized blacksmith tools: tongs and a hammer each as long as a boat, blackened and worn, plus a giant reel of hair-thin molten metal thread. HANDLING: he sets the teapot down before working and picks it up after; he drinks a sip so small it cannot be seen to change the level. The contrast between his enormous hands and this fragile object is the whole character, so the teapot must never be handled roughly and must never break. Never add: a giant-sized teapot (it must be human-sized or the joke and the tenderness both die), decoration, gold, a cup, anyone else drinking.
```

name: Le Gantelet Vieilli De Lanterne
text:
```
Object: the right gauntlet of Lanterne, in two ages. Before the rib bridge: a small articulated knight's gauntlet in ivory and warm pale-gray plate, worn but well kept, the wrist opening showing only darkness ,  this armor is empty, there is no hand inside. After the Passant: the exact same gauntlet suddenly a century older ,  the polish completely gone, the surface pitted and eaten with corrosion, brown rust blooming in uneven patches, the leather straps dried and cracked, one rivet blackened and missing so a plate hangs slightly loose. STATE RULE: the aging is PERMANENT and takes about a second and a half to happen on screen. From that moment to the end of the episode and beyond, this gauntlet stays old, and it GRINDS audibly when the hand closes. It is never repaired ,  not by Bourdon, not by anyone. CONTINUITY RULE: only this one gauntlet ages. The rest of the armor stays pale and clean, and the contrast between the two hands must be readable even in a wide shot. Never add: rust spreading to the rest of the armor, restoration, a matching aged left gauntlet, a hand or skin inside, blood.
```

name: La Botte Du Suiveur
text:
```
Object: a pair of heavily worn medieval leather traveler boots, soft and shapeless from years of walking, the seams split and clumsily restitched, the sole worn thin and unevenly at the heel, mud dried into the creases, and one toe distinctly scuffed pale. A poor man's boots, repaired many times and never replaced. FUNCTION RULE: this object exists for RECOGNITION and nothing else. It appears alone in the corner of a frame at the end of the first sequence, with its owner entirely out of shot, and it must be identifiable again several sequences later on the foot of a man hanging upside down. The scuffed toe is the recognition point and must be visible in both appearances, at the same angle if possible. HANDLING: it is set down silently, deliberately ,  this man is a professional shadow. Never add: armor, spurs, cleanliness, newness, a matching pair in good condition, any emblem.
```

name: Le Caillou De Lanterne
text:
```
Object: one small ordinary pebble the size of a walnut, smooth and rounded, pale grey with one distinctive darker vein running across it and one small chipped facet on a corner. Nothing magical, nothing glowing, nothing precious ,  an entirely ordinary stone. FUNCTION RULE: a small tender character beat, and it must be EXACTLY THE SAME STONE whenever it appears ,  the vein and the chipped corner are the recognition points. HANDLING (Ep2): Lanterne picks it up out of pure curiosity in sequence 2 and hides it hastily in a joint of his armor when he thinks he is being told off; it makes a small rattling noise inside the armor from then on. He simply KEEPS it ,  the payoff is saved for a later episode. Never add: glow, value, magical property, a second stone, engraving, losing it.
```

name: Les Lanternes Du Pont
text:
```
Object: old medieval iron hanging lanterns along the rib bridge ,  square, with four small dirty glass panes and a hinged top, hanging from chains on hand-forged hooks at uneven intervals. STATE RULE: they are EXTINGUISHED, always, and have been for centuries. No flame, no candle left inside, the glass grimed and clouded, the iron dark with age. They are never lit, in any shot, at any point. SECOND STATE, for the Passant scene only: as the time field passes over them, rust runs across the iron like flame across paper, spreads to the chain and the hook, the glass frosts and crazes ,  and then it all reverses completely once the field has moved on, back to exactly the previous state. MEANING, never spoken: someone once lit this road, and no one has for a very long time. Never add: a flame, a candle, any light inside, a modern lamp, evenly spaced hanging, a lantern that stays rusted after the field passes.
```

name: La Hallebarde Des Écaillés
text:
```
Object: a tall polearm whose head is carved from polished dark STONE rather than forged from metal ,  a heavy asymmetrical blade with a hooked spur, chipped along the edge, bound to a long dark wooden shaft with leather cord and sinew. Sober, functional, kept with ceremonial care, and genuinely lethal. VARIETY RULE, which matters as much as the design: these are hand-made and NO TWO ARE IDENTICAL. Whenever several appear, their blade shapes, lengths and bindings must visibly differ, and they must never be held at the same angle or evenly spaced ,  the same anti-clone rule that governs the Écaillés themselves. HANDLING: carried upright at rest; lowered in a loose irregular arc when the court closes in, never in a drilled military line. Never add: metal blades, gold, engraving, identical copies, perfect formation, even spacing, banners on the shafts.
```

name: Le Cercle De Fer Du Roi Voûte
text:
```
Object: a very simple hand-forged iron circlet, a plain unadorned band, slightly irregular in thickness, still showing the hammer marks of whoever made it, darkened with age and polished bright only where it has rubbed against a skull for centuries. No jewels, no gold, no points, no engraving, no ornament of any kind. MEANING: the humility of it is the entire point ,  this king rules a thousand-year-old people and wears a band a blacksmith made in an afternoon. HANDLING: never removed, never adjusted, never touched by anyone. It sits slightly off-center on his cracked crest because his skull is not symmetrical. Never add: gold, jewels, points, spikes, engraving, a second crown, any religious symbol.
```

name: La Moitié D'Une Promesse⚠️
text:
```
⚠️ Statut à trancher : la Bible des Objets dit que cette demi-clé est ramassée par Lanterne à l'épisode 2, mais elle n'apparaît pas dans le scénario V2 ,  le caillou a pris sa place. Fiche fournie, à n'activer que si tu la réinjectes (le meilleur endroit serait l'établi de Bourdon, séquence 5).

Object: half of an old iron key, broken LENGTHWISE down its middle rather than snapped across, so the shaft is split along its length and only one half of the bit remains. Hand-forged and slightly crude, blackened with age, the broken edge clean and old and worn smooth by handling. A single simple abstract symbol is stamped into the bow ,  a mark, never letters, never numbers, never writing of any kind. MEANING, never explained on screen: a smith spent forty years forging the same key, again and again, and none of them opened anything. This one, perhaps. The other half is missing, and so is the door. HANDLING: small enough to disappear into a joint of armor, and it makes a different sound from the pebble. Never add: letters, numbers, runes, writing, glow, a complete key, a second half, a lock.
```

---

name: Barrik
text:
```
HEAD RULE, ABSOLUTE: Barrik HAS NO HEAD AND NO HELM. Nothing sits on top of him. His barrel IS his head and his body at once, and his EYES ARE SIMPLY TWO HOLES IN THE BARREL ITSELF ,  dark openings in the wood-and-metal shell, nothing more. Never give him a helmet, never a lantern head, never a dome, never anything perched on top; never borrow Lanterne's lantern helmet or any part of it. Behavior and acting: an empty knight armor shaped like a squat, round WINE BARREL ,  his silhouette alone is instantly readable as a headless barrel with stubby arms and legs and two eye-holes in its face; Frank's own reference sheet is the ONLY source of his exact design, copy it exactly, no reinterpretation. He is, by his own Order's reputation, THE WORST KNIGHT WHO EVER LIVED: cowardly, clumsy, easily panicked, comic relief through and through ,  but never cruel comedy, never humiliating, just a lovable disaster. He runs in a frantic waddling scramble, arms pinwheeling, when frightened ,  which is often. His signature defense: he can pull his limbs fully inside his barrel-shaped shell like a tortoise, sealing himself in ,  and once safely inside, his bravado returns instantly, taunting whatever just scared him. He is an EMPTY armor like Lanterne and Serrure: no face, no mouth, nothing inside; when he speaks nothing on him moves at all ,  no jaw, no helm, no head ,  the voice simply comes out of the barrel, hollow and metallic, but HIGHER-PITCHED and reedier than Serrure's, quick, nervy, blustery ,  brave only in retrospect or from complete safety. Serrure knows him as an old acquaintance from the Order and finds him hilarious rather than pathetic ,  genuine affection under the mockery. Keep him gentle and silly, never grotesque, never truly at risk.
```
